name: Iron Gear
description: Iron Gear's surface is dominated by immense circular mountain ranges that spiral outward from the planet's equator like the teeth of some colossal mechanism. Russet-colored plains stretch between the ridges, interrupted by crystalline cavern systems that refract the amber sunlight into prismatic arcs. The sky shifts from copper at dawn to deep indigo at dusk, streaked with thin cirrus clouds that move in eerily regular patterns.

Standing on the surface, one feels the low hum of tectonic activity reverberating through the ground, a rhythm so steady it resembles the ticking of a vast clock. The air carries a faint metallic tang mixed with the sweetness of the broad-leafed flora that carpets the rift valleys. Seasonal shifts are subtle but precise, the planet tilting on its axis with almost mechanical regularity.

The spiral mountain formations have long puzzled geologists, their too-perfect curvature suggesting forces beyond natural tectonics. Deep within the crystal caverns, explorers have found ruins carved from an unknown alloy, their surfaces inscribed with gear-like symbols that predate any known civilization. A persistent low-frequency signal emanates from somewhere beneath the equatorial ridge, defying all attempts at triangulation.

Iron Gear draws prospectors for its rich titanium deposits and xenoarchaeologists hoping to decode the ruins beneath the mountains. The signal has intensified in recent decades, and some researchers believe it may be a countdown. Whatever mechanism lies buried here, it appears to be winding toward activation, and no one can say what it will set in motion.
